title: A change of plan

fn.en: Change arrangements; write a professional email.

gr: the language of changing an arrangement, by phone and by email

sub.en: You are moving a meeting. Choose the version that keeps the relationship intact.

items.q: You are opening the phone call.
o: There’s been a change of plan.
There has become a change of plan.
It has a change of plan.

items.q: You are saying why, without giving a life story.
o: I’m afraid I’ve got something else on tomorrow lunchtime.
I’m afraid I have something else on tomorrow lunchtime, because my aunt…
I am afraid to have something else tomorrow.

items.q: You are suggesting an alternative time, informally.
o: How about getting together after work instead?
How about to get together after work instead?
How about we getting together after work?
items.why: How about + -ing, or How about we + verb. Not an infinitive.

items.q: You have an arrangement you may be able to move.
o: I’m supposed to be playing tennis, but I can probably change it.
I’m supposed to playing tennis, but I can probably change it.
I suppose to play tennis, but I can probably change it.
items.why: be supposed to + infinitive; the continuous shows an arrangement already made.

items.q: You cannot do the time they suggested.
o: I’m really sorry, but I can’t make it then.
I’m really sorry, but I can’t make it that.
I’m really sorry, but I don’t can make it then.

items.q: You are asking formally whether a change is possible.
o: Would it be possible to move our meeting to Friday?
Would it be possible moving our meeting to Friday?
Would be it possible to move our meeting to Friday?

items.q: You are promising to come back to them.
o: I’ll speak to her and get back to you.
I’ll speak to her and get back at you.
I speak to her and get back to you.

items.q: You are closing the email politely.
o: Apologies for any inconvenience this may cause.
Apologies for any inconvenience this may make.
Apologies of any inconvenience this may cause.

acts.title: To: e.tulegenova@bmk.kz
text: Subject: Thursday’s review meeting — proposed new time
I am afraid I have to ask you to change the time of Thursday’s review meeting.
A clash has come up in my diary: I have been asked to attend the regional audit on the same morning, and I am not able to move it.

Would it be possible to reschedule for Friday at 10:00, or for Thursday at 16:00 if Friday does not suit you? I am available at both times and I have already checked that the small meeting room is free.
Apologies for any inconvenience this may cause. I would be grateful if you could confirm which of the two works better for you.

items.r: says what has changed before the email is opened
gives the bad news immediately, without a long build-up
gives the reason in a single sentence
apologizes and asks for a decision

items.q: Which three words soften the bad news in the first line?
Which five words ask formally about the change? (Would it … ?)
Which one word means “arrange for a different time”?
Which two words open the apology?
Which three words ask her to reply? (I would be … )

acts.genre: Register · a call or an email
acts.title: Would you phone or write?
text: A phone call is quicker and warmer, and lets you agree a new time in one go. You can be direct: “How about Thursday?”
An email leaves a record, which is what a client or a manager needs. It gives the reason once, offers alternatives and asks for confirmation.

Actually, that’s why I’m phoning. There’s been a change of plan. I’m afraid I’ve got something else on tomorrow lunchtime — a work meeting from twelve till two that I can’t change. So how about getting together after work instead? Say six?

No problem. I’ll speak to you later, then.

write.q: Write a professional email of about 120 words moving a meeting, an appointment or a delivery. Follow the model: subject line → the change → the reason in one line → two alternatives → apology and a request to confirm.
write.model:
Subject: Wednesday’s handover session — proposed new time

Dear Aizhan,

I am afraid I have to ask you to move Wednesday’s handover session.

A clash has come up: I have been asked to travel to the Temirtau site on the same day, and the visit cannot be rearranged.

Would it be possible to reschedule for Thursday at 11:00, or for Monday at 15:00 if Thursday does not suit you? I am available at both times, and I have already asked Marat whether he can join us on either.

Apologies for any inconvenience this may cause. I would be grateful if you could confirm which of the two works better for you.

Best regards,
Tilek

speak.q: Now make the same change by phone. Say it out loud: break the news, give the reason in one sentence, suggest an alternative, react when the other person cannot do it, and agree what happens next.
speak.model: Hi Aizhan, it’s Tilek. Look, I’m afraid there’s been a change of plan about Wednesday — I’ve been asked to go out to Temirtau that day and I can’t move it. How about Thursday morning instead? … Ah, you can’t make eleven. Would Monday afternoon be possible? … Right. I’m supposed to be finishing the report on Monday, but I can probably move that. Let me check with Marat and I’ll get back to you today.
